Works with

Rugged tablet for IFS Ultimo

IFS Ultimo is a cloud-based Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) and CMMS platform used by maintenance, facilities, fleet and HSE teams in manufacturing, food and beverage, chemicals, healthcare, logistics and utilities. The vendor has a UK office in Staines and publishes UK customer cases including London Gatwick Airport, Victrex, National Grid Nemo Link, the Manufacturing Technology Centre and Bristol Port Company. The field app is Ultimo Go+, published by IFS Ultimo B.V. for Android and iOS.

On the floor or on site, technicians use Ultimo Go+ to process activities and inspections, report new activities, look up equipment, inventory, buildings, suppliers and contracts, attach photos from the camera, use GPS, and scan QR codes and barcodes. The vendor states the app keeps working when the device is temporarily disconnected. That means the device is in use in plant rooms, on gantries, in vehicles and outdoors, where a tablet without an ingress rating or a drop rating is at more risk of damage than it would be at a desk.

This page sets out what the vendor publishes about device requirements for Ultimo Go+, which Tuga device fits those requirements, where the Windows option does and does not apply, and how UK business buyers can trial one unit before ordering a fleet.

Requirements

What IFS Ultimo (Ultimo Go+ mobile app) needs from a device

Each item below comes from IFS Ultimo B.V.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 8.0 and up for the Ultimo Go+ app

    The Google Play listing for Ultimo Go+ (package com.ultimo.UltimoGoPlus, developer IFS Ultimo B.V.) requires Android 8.0 and up. The Tuga A10 and Tuga A6 run Android 14, which meets this requirement. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline working

    The Play and App Store listings state: "Even if you are temporarily disconnected, you can continue working." and list "Available offline: working without an internet connection" as a feature. The vendor's Ultimo Mobile page states that offline working requires Ultimo Go+ rather than the online-only Ultimo Go. The vendor does not publish how much data is cached or how sync conflicts are handled. Source: play.google.com

  • Camera for QR and barcode scanning and for photos

    The app lists "Scanning (QR code, barcode)" and "Camera integration (linking photos)" as features. No dedicated scan engine or scanner SDK requirement is published, so scanning is done through the device camera. Source: apps.apple.com

  • GPS

    The Play listing lists "GPS integration" as a feature of Ultimo Go+, so a device with a GPS receiver is needed to use it. Source: play.google.com

  • Windows: desktop web client only, no Windows build of Ultimo Go+

    The vendor's Ultimo Mobile page states that Ultimo Go+ is available "via the Apple Store (iOS) or the Google Play Store (Android)". No Windows app or Microsoft Store listing was found. The vendor's CMMS page describes the system as a cloud-based solution running on Microsoft Azure, accessed from desktop and mobile devices, and does not publish a supported-browser list or PC requirements. Source: ultimo.com

  • NFC and RFID: not listed as Ultimo Go+ features

    The current Google Play and App Store descriptions, the App Store release history and the public ultimo.com pages we checked do not list NFC or RFID tag reading among Ultimo Go+ features. We do not claim it works. If tag reading matters to you, confirm it with IFS Ultimo before buying. The NFC on Tuga devices is a hardware fact only. Source: apps.apple.com

  • No published hardware or screen-size guidance

    IFS Ultimo publishes no recommended devices, hardware requirements or screen-size guidance on its public pages; its Ultimo Mobile page says "Contact us for the required hardware and software" and describes using the app "on your tablet or smartphone". The only published requirements are the store minimums (Android 8.0 and up; iOS/iPadOS 15.0 or later). The cloud page states only that the mobile app "runs with the minimum privileges required on the operating system." Source: ultimo.com

The vendor publishes Ultimo Go+ for Android and iOS only, so the Tuga W10 cannot run the field app; it is suitable only for the browser-based desktop client, and IFS Ultimo publishes no supported-browser list or PC requirements. The W10's optional 2D barcode scanner and optional UHF RFID reader do not help with Ultimo Go+ because the app does not run on Windows. Scanning in Ultimo Go+ is through the camera. The A10 and A6 both have rear cameras, but neither has a dedicated scan engine, so scanning depends on the app's camera support. The vendor publishes no recommended devices, so none of the devices on this page is tested, approved or certified by IFS Ultimo.
Setting up

Getting IFS Ultimo (Ultimo Go+ mobile app) running

  1. Confirm with your IFS Ultimo administrator that your edition and user licences cover the technicians who will use Ultimo Go+, and that mobile access is enabled for their accounts.
  2. On the Tuga A10 or A6, sign in to a Google account, open Google Play, search for Ultimo Go+ (publisher IFS Ultimo B.V.) and install it. Android 14 on both devices meets the app's Android 8.0 and up requirement.
  3. Open the app and sign in with the credentials and environment details your administrator provides.
  4. Before the first shift, open the app on Wi-Fi and let it download its data, then test it with Wi-Fi and mobile data switched off to confirm the offline working described by the vendor behaves as you expect for your data volume.
  5. Grant camera and location permissions when the app asks, then test a QR or barcode scan on an existing asset label and a photo attachment on a test activity.
  6. Fit the hand strap (A10, in the box) or tempered glass screen protector, and add a vehicle mounting dock or charging dock where the device will live between jobs.
